_comment: sg13g2-bandgap -- record spec for closed-loop-psrr-pex on the `klt sim`
harness (issue #278). The per-experiment half of the adapter contract:
sim/harness/klt_sim_evidence.py owns the record MECHANICS and takes
every piece of ARGUMENT from this file.
Claim: Closed-loop power-supply rejection of the assembled bandgap across the full PVT grid, through the same generated PEX DUT as sim/closed-loop-vref-pvt-pex's klt bench (every device's geometry and every wire parasitic from #380's re-extraction of the trim-bearing layout/bandgap_top.gds, PR #383): a 1 V/0 deg AC perturbation on vdd with the loop closed, PSRR = -db(v(vref)), the operating point nodeset-seeded from sim/closed-loop-startup's committed record (125 C row per corner/supply baked -- the worst-corner stiffness -- with the enrichment pass checking the landed op against the per-temperature reference from that same record with the hand-transcribed bench's own 50 mV tolerance, plus startup-released / loop-closed / not-railed). Every column is expected to sit near the 2026-10-04 record's values: PR #383 drew the PDK runset's recognition layers in the HV MOS and npn13G2 helpers, which permuted the per-device bulk hub tags and gave the resistor cards their L/W geometry but left the parasitic network's size unchanged (842 wire resistors and 261 capacitors, as in #272's extraction), so this re-run tests that the re-drawn recognition layers did not move the measured rejection -- it is not expected to. NOT a claim against any ratified spec row.
Netlist provenance: layout/bandgap_top/bandgap_top.pex.spice (#380's re-extraction of the trim-bearing layout, PR #383) + design/netlist/bandgap_core.spice, design/netlist/bandgap_amp.spice and design/netlist/bandgap_startup.spice (the top netlist's three subckts, flattened through its own Xx1/Xx2/Xx3 instance lines by sim/tools/gen_pex_netlist_body.py --cell top -- the DUT body is generated, never hand-transcribed, and the flattened instance set is what D2 compares).
PDK: `ihp-sg13g2` -- pinned release in sim/pdk.json; OSDI models built by sim/tools/build-osdi.sh (local) / baked into the batch runner image (#277).
Corner matrix run: process {typ,bcs,wcs,sf,fs} x temperature {-40,27,125} C x supply {2.97,3.30,3.63} V (45 points)
